properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-09-14.

═══ THE IDEA, in his words ═══

"could purposefully have a '/template' type skill that the user can define a building block of the systems - could have /building-block or /interface or /contract or /function or any number of skills that allow the user to purposefully define a systems engineering unit for a particular domain. These could even be skills the agent uses that have SE definitions that automatically label or help the agent translate SE to the domain the user is working in. I'm not sure from a reflow2 perspective if you could have some fixed tools that are simply SE definitions or labels for the agent so that it can quickly assign to them to a description."

═══ ⭐ THE TWO FACES, AND WHY THEY ARE ONE QUESTION ═══

He describes the same mechanism pointed in two directions, and said so himself ("could even be skills the agent uses"):

**USER-FACING** — `/function`, `/interface`, `/contract`, `/building-block`. The user says *"this is a function"* deliberately, instead of the agent inferring it from their phrasing. It is the user taking the routing decision ON PURPOSE, at a moment when they have the thing in mind.

**AGENT-FACING** — a fixed, served set of SE definitions the agent can assign quickly: *what an Interface IS*, in one authoritative sentence, so the agent labels a description against a definition rather than against its own priors.

═══ ⚠️ THE OBJECTION THAT HAS TO BE FACED FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE PROJECT'S OWN DOCTRINE ═══

**capture-intent says, in bold: "Never ask the user which node type to use."** It says handing that question back "gives the one person in the room with no reason to know the answer the one decision they cannot check", and there is a shipped check (`ver:the-capture-skills-do-not-hand-the-vocabulary-back`) enforcing it. The user-facing half of this idea is, on its face, exactly the thing that rule forbids.

**The honest counter, and it may be strong enough**: there is a difference between the agent ASKING the user to pick a type, and the user CHOOSING to declare one. The rule was written against the first. A user typing `/interface` has volunteered; a user being asked "is this an Interface or a Capability?" has been handed work. Whether that distinction survives contact with a non-SE user is exactly what is open — because Alex, who is technical, hit this and wrote a translator rather than answering.

**And the rule's own evidence cuts both ways**: it came from a first-time user who was asked what node types to store his data models as, said "you figure it out", and it worked. That user DECLINED to declare. This idea assumes users who want to.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) NOTHING — the doctrine already settles it.** The agent routes; the user never picks. ⚠️ Counter: it settles the user-facing half and says nothing about the agent-facing half, which no rule forbids and which nothing serves today.

**(b) THE AGENT-FACING HALF ONLY — served SE definitions the agent labels against.** This is the half with no doctrinal conflict, and it has a measured hole behind it: `dec:idea-does-the-black-box-frame-reach-the-agent-at-call-time` found the translate-to-the-user lens on 2 of 177 tools and the black-box frame in no served instruction. ⚠️ Counter: `describe_schema` already returns the vocabulary, so this may be a delivery problem dressed as a missing feature — the definitions exist and nothing points the agent at them at the right moment.

**(c) BOTH, with the user-facing half framed as OPT-IN DECLARATION rather than a question.** ⚠️ Counter: a dozen new slash commands is a large surface for a mechanism whose need is measured on one or two users, and every one of them is a door a confused user can walk through wrongly. `/interface` typed by somebody who means "the screen" would write a category error with full confidence and no ambiguity flag.

**(d) ONE skill, not a family — `/declare` or `/template`, which asks what kind of unit this is.** Smaller surface, same effect. ⚠️ Counter: loses the thing that makes the family attractive — that `/function` is guessable and self-documenting where `/declare` is not.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

Whether any user has ever WANTED to declare a type. Alex did the opposite — he wrote a translator so he would not have to, and reflow2's own recorded evidence has a user explicitly refusing ("you figure it out"). **Nobody has yet been observed reaching for a `/function` that was not there**, which is the signal `report_manual_work` exists to catch. Until one is, (b) is the half standing on measured ground and the rest is a hypothesis.
properties.name: OPEN — should a user be able to DECLARE a systems-engineering unit on purpose (/function, /interface, /contract, /building-block), and is the agent-facing mirror — fixed SE labels it assigns — the same mechanism or a different one?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as an open question via the brainstorm discipline. The doctrinal objection is stated at full strength rather than softened, because it is a shipped, lint-checked rule of this project and any answer here has to get past it or change it deliberately.

Kept as ONE decision rather than two because Anthony framed the two faces as one mechanism in one breath, and separating them would lose the thing he noticed — that the same SE definitions serve the user declaring and the agent labelling.
